expression.original: In the G4 model, observer independence is an angle, not a bit. Sweeping the angle between two projection directions over a 20x20 grid, mean ambiguity averaged over all 400 hidden truths falls smoothly: 80.00 (one view alone), 60.00 at 0 degrees, 46.59 at 15, 32.38 at 30, 24.53 at 45, 18.98 at 75, 20.00 at 90. Three consequences. (1) Even a fully correlated second view (0 degrees, same direction) narrows ambiguity if its granularity differs, so CLM-0014's 'adds nothing' is the limiting case of identical direction AND identical partition, not of shared direction alone. (2) Partial independence buys most of the benefit: 45 degrees already achieves 24.53 of a best-possible 18.98. (3) The mean-optimal angle (75 degrees, mean 18.98, worst 21) differs from the worst-case-optimal angle (90 degrees, mean 20.00, worst 20) - which criterion 'best observer diversity' means is itself a projection choice, i.e. G2's mean-blindness applies to the evaluation of G4 itself.
expression.elaboration: First lab-to-field promotion. The computation lives in lab/julia/angle_sweep.jl; it averages over every hidden truth to avoid the single-point aliasing that made an earlier sweep non-monotonic.

context.position: lab result promoted to field observation; refines CLM-0013/CLM-0014 quantitatively

distinctions: correlated direction vs identical partition - only the second makes an observer's contribution vacuous
mean-case diversity vs worst-case diversity - they select different optimal configurations
a lab result (runnable, unreviewed-as-claim) vs a field observation (this record) - the promotion is the boundary crossing
